<clause id="_fe734889-68b9-1a95-1e5b-c1b7fb099480" obligation="informative">
<title id="_99cc30d8-d61a-5e83-e834-c1781b03070f">GeoSciML Basic and Extension</title>
<p id="_47feb332-b64c-0983-e408-d342b9b2b5af">GeoSciML describes geological features from the mapping perspective, articulated around the concept of a MappedFeature – the cartographic element shown on a map, and the GeologicFeature it represents.  All geologic concepts that can be represented on a map are subtypes of GeologicFeature.</p>

<figure id="_bb86a476-a6f5-ac1e-45ba-20fb269c3157" anchor="img_highlevel_model" width="562">
2



000582_d8cd2523-08f9-e1a8-dce0-f8d6b7c28f76STANDOC_48
(generic warning) Hanging paragraph in clause
<clause id="_d8cd2523-08f9-e1a8-dce0-f8d6b7c28f76" obligation="normative">
<title id="_3e845d00-ba58-ead2-fcd1-9602cabe7a90">Logical Model</title>
<p id="_5ca9713c-f6ac-8ce3-ea6c-360da301b6c9">This section describes requirements that must be met by all target implementations that claim conformance to this specification.  The target implementation of the logical model is generally an encoding specification or a schema (which could use technologies like XSD, for example) and not a data instance.  The logical model, expressed using UML, provides naming, structure and cardinality for any physical implementation.  The UML model is a normative artefact as the official representation of GeoSciML.  Rules that can be unambiguously inferred from the UML model will not be documented as explicit requirements.  Specific encoding idiosyncrasies shall be addressed in the requirement clauses pertaining to that encoding.</p>

<p id="_4b60ae41-bc41-0eea-d1ba-bca25fe549f7">The logical model contains almost no semantic requirements (i.e., vocabularies, enumerations).  It is expected that users will employ controlled vocabularies of terms which are developed by user communities.  The model provides mechanisms for delivering concepts from controlled vocabularies via URI’s and linked data principles.</p>
2



000588_60a6d584-24a4-e8fe-2977-ac0e7404c7bdSTANDOC_48
(generic warning) Hanging paragraph in clause
<clause id="_60a6d584-24a4-e8fe-2977-ac0e7404c7bd" obligation="normative">
<title id="_a5cbb3f5-e096-58b4-3202-d68b888e9078">UML Model</title>
<p id="_ba3fe303-8fec-a407-45a5-288748f0b3ca">The UML model provides name, structure and cardinality for data elements composing various potential physical implementations of GeoSciML.  There are formal mappings between UML and GML (ISO-19136), UML and RDF (ISO-19150) and best practices exist for mapping UML to RDBMS.  Although it is assumed that UML is technologically neutral, in reality UML models always end up addressing some of the encoding specification details.  The current GeoSciML UML model has been designed as a GML application according to ISO 19109 and borrows some of artefacts of GML. Several design decisions were guided by limitations of UML (e.g. single inheritance) and XSD (package dependencies artefacts) and some constraints of GML delivery using ISO19142 WFS (for instance, some XSD encodings are not queryable easily with ISO19143 FES).  However, the UML model is detailed enough to constrain the main elements of any encoding; the names of entities and the cardinality of properties, the associations between entities and to some extent property types.  On the other hand, some UML features do not have equivalences in certain encoding (for instance, JSON does not have a native support for namespaces or even schema).</p>

<p id="_1aea14a0-271d-630a-165d-31c3832c14b9"> <xref target="img_logical_model_req_dep"/> shows requirements class dependencies:</p>
2



000600_eaf14142-4372-7190-a7b7-f8a65db46a7fSTANDOC_48
(generic warning) Hanging paragraph in clause
<clause id="_eaf14142-4372-7190-a7b7-f8a65db46a7f" obligation="normative">
<title id="_79faa6d7-e3cf-1eb8-b9f8-24be6601ff61">Property cardinality</title>
<p id="_81922e72-cb3c-cbd3-39a7-b4ef5dc88807">All properties that could feasibly be made optional are optional in GeoSciML 4.1.  This is a reversal of the pattern used in GeoSciML version 3.2 where all properties were made mandatory, forcing the data provider to document why the property was missing using nillable properties.  This design attracted a lot of criticism (not only for GeoSciML but for other communities confronted with the same pattern) from application developers and data providers that consider filling the instance with nil properties is “unnecessarily verbose” and a waste of bandwidth.  It has been argued that nillable properties are just verbose absent values.  This issue is a real concern for mobile applications where payload has an impact on user experience.</p>

<p id="_066bd942-04a1-dac9-1638-bd2b805afe62">Nillable properties actually carry useful or even required information in certain use cases, such as legally bounded data exchange scenarios.  Some communities using GeoSciML may still want to force usage of nillable properties and the SWG recognised that different communities might want to enforce the use of some properties for their particular needs.  To meet this requirement and to offer flexibility to various communities wanting to use (or extend) GeoSciML, properties are optional, but can still be nilled.  A data provider is offered two options when a value is missing:</p>
2

000784_ff654441-1c0d-7291-0f9e-7aa4aa1928ddSTANDOC_48

<clause id="_ff654441-1c0d-7291-0f9e-7aa4aa1928dd" obligation="normative">
<title id="_b03eee68-01c2-d8a5-52db-f068c2e9197e">Geology Basic</title>
<p id="_340dc971-8644-96d5-30d3-eba4a8794237">GeologyBasic is a package of classes representing fundamental geological map features and the relations between them.  GeoSciML describes a geologic dataset as a series of GeologicFeature occurrences, spatially represented as MappedFeature.  A map is a collection of MappedFeatures.  The term “map”, typically understood as a map sheet (a given area on the surface of the earth), is only one of the possible collection of MappedFeatures.  Other examples are cross-sections, block diagrams, and even borehole logs (a linear map).  MappedFeature can represent any features and GeologicFeatures are one of the kinds of features it can represent.  A MappedFeature identifies what it represents using its “specification” association. </p>

<p id="_26dfd81b-d53e-fda4-f769-8812d650a1f1"> <xref target="img_geologic_feature_and_mappedfeature"/> shows the fundamental relationships between a MappedFeature and the GeologicFeature.  GeologicFeature is further subtyped into GeologicUnit, GeologicStructure, GeomorphologicFeature and GeologicEvent.</p>
2



000794_cdc2b6c2-a000-1271-b6dd-67811dbe8d45STANDOC_48
(generic warning) Hanging paragraph in clause
<clause id="_cdc2b6c2-a000-1271-b6dd-67811dbe8d45" obligation="normative">
<title id="_9bdcc6b8-ed69-e856-1707-7a5c18440268">GeologicFeature</title>
<p id="_f26dbfb8-ff55-cbce-fe65-d42a32839368">The abstract GeologicFeature class represents a conceptual feature that is hypothesized to exist coherently in the world.  It corresponds with a “legend item” from a traditional geologic map and its instance acts as the “description package”.  The description package is classified according to its intended purpose as a <em>typicalNorm</em>, <em>definingNorm or instance</em>.  GeologicFeature can be used outside the context of a map (it can lack a MappedFeature), for example when describing typical norms (describing expected property from a feature) or defining norms (describing properties required from a feature to be classifying in a group, such as given geologic unit).  A GeologicFeature appearing on a map is considered as an “instance”.</p>

<figure id="_abfb4747-0841-a43a-1e67-fd42d610ce82" anchor="img_geologic_feature_context_diagram" width="601">
2



000859_8595366c-34ac-117b-dd7d-d1edebac90e3STANDOC_48
(generic warning) Hanging paragraph in clause
<clause id="_8595366c-34ac-117b-dd7d-d1edebac90e3" obligation="normative">
<title id="_eb3194b1-05a5-41ea-f795-94f244ad884a">MappedFeature</title>
<p id="_c10fc99d-1c58-b1d6-9e20-c2d97a89a208">A MappedFeature is part of a geological interpretation. It provides a link between a notional feature (description package) and one spatial representation of it, or part of it (exposures, surface traces and intercepts, etc.).  The mapped features are the elements that compose a map, a cross-section, a borehole log, or any other representation.  The mappingFrame identifies the domain being mapped by the geometries.  For typical geological maps, the mapping frame is the surface of the earth (the 2.5D interface between the surface of the bedrock and whatever sits on it; atmosphere or overburden material for bedrock maps).  It can also be abstract frames, such as the arbitrary plane that forms a mine level or a cross-section, the 3D volume enclosing an ore body or the line that approximate the path of a borehole.</p>

<p id="_3ce75c97-1b78-80e1-5c04-5095d19a7ecc">The specification association identifies what notional feature is being mapped.  It can be any features and is not restricted to GeoSciML feature, although it is expected to be for geological maps.</p>
2



000898_cb085edc-e0ba-fba2-0de5-a69650592645STANDOC_48
(generic warning) Hanging paragraph in clause
<clause id="_cb085edc-e0ba-fba2-0de5-a69650592645" obligation="normative">
<title id="_b84ece52-6981-60b1-e673-6e382813e301">GeologicUnit</title>
<p id="_aa29f7d7-517a-352a-7029-7c4135bd4516">Conceptually, a GeologicUnit may represent a body of material in the Earth whose complete and precise extent is inferred to exist (e.g., North American Data Model GeologicUnit [12], Stratigraphic unit in the sense of NACSN [14], or International Stratigraphic Code [9]), or a classifier used to characterize parts of the Earth (e.g. lithologic map unit like ‘granitic rock’ or ‘alluvial deposit’, surficial units like ‘till’ or ‘old alluvium’). It includes both formal units (i.e. formally adopted and named in an official lexicon) and informal units (i.e. named but not promoted to a lexicon) and unnamed units (i.e., recognizable, described and delineable in the field but not otherwise formalised).  In simpler terms, a geologic unit is a package of earth material (generally rock).</p>

<figure id="_9b672430-f498-2389-0138-1a80d6b43dc4" anchor="img_geologicunit_context_diagram" width="601">
2



000943_430496ac-f305-0a9e-6e55-58e14b137b7dSTANDOC_48
(generic warning) Hanging paragraph in clause
<clause id="_430496ac-f305-0a9e-6e55-58e14b137b7d" obligation="normative">
<title id="_e2a3c673-b0ea-e5df-6510-b9175bc2bedb">GeologicUnitHierarchy</title>
<p id="_d8ecc11f-b67d-5e01-6541-e987998d16d3">GeologicUnitHierarchy associates a GeologicUnit with another GeologicUnit that is a proper part of that unit. Parts may be formal or notional. Formal parts refer to a specific body of rock, as in formal stratigraphic members. Notional parts refer to assemblages of particular EarthMaterials with particular internal structure, which may be repeated in various places within a unit (e.g. ‘turbidite sequence’, ‘point bar assemblage’, ‘leucosome veins’). </p>

<clause id="_1cb223e3-9f4e-760a-3a14-66f470bf70f9" obligation="normative">
2



000963_7274aa61-caf3-c9f8-85fc-dbeb6db9646cSTANDOC_48
(generic warning) Hanging paragraph in clause
<clause id="_7274aa61-caf3-c9f8-85fc-dbeb6db9646c" obligation="normative">
<title id="_3154a0dd-2c2d-6091-8ef0-67c9d847884d">CompositionPart</title>
<p id="_f47b6b47-c05e-da0c-39ab-11990afe4a59">CompositionPart represents the composition of a geologic unit in terms of earth material constituents (CompoundMaterial).  It decomposes the material making of the unit into parts having distinct roles and proportions.</p>

<clause id="_642512a3-10d5-798e-9761-153efade15b6" obligation="normative">
2



000983_389b08ea-1883-9932-9b13-fe5eafd78f1bSTANDOC_48
(generic warning) Hanging paragraph in clause
<clause id="_389b08ea-1883-9932-9b13-fe5eafd78f1b" obligation="normative">
<title id="_755533b3-af62-e8f4-1e81-858e93d9868f">EarthMaterial</title>
<p id="_e3a651c4-2045-abbb-6bb5-6c2df9407637">The EarthMaterial class holds a description of a naturally occurring substance in the Earth.  EarthMaterial represents material composition or substance, and is thus independent of quantity or location. Ideally, EarthMaterials are defined strictly based on physical properties, but because of standard geological usage, genetic interpretations enter into the description as well.  </p>

<figure id="_14f5f3b7-06b5-d771-f252-6385dac3ae7d" anchor="img_earthmaterial_and_related_classes" width="516">
2



001016_0ddaf658-2475-0e09-0f36-b49f9d4a4c70STANDOC_48
(generic warning) Hanging paragraph in clause
<clause id="_0ddaf658-2475-0e09-0f36-b49f9d4a4c70" obligation="normative">
<title id="_07e5a807-f793-67d4-b62a-a5ae13a13afb">RockMaterial</title>
<p id="_6d4398f0-1940-9d43-360c-8bfc7293782d">RockMaterial is a specialized CompoundMaterial that includes consolidated and unconsolidated materials (such as surficial sediments) as well as mixtures of consolidated and unconsolidated materials.  In GeoSciML Basic, Rock Material is essentially a link to a controlled vocabulary (lithology property) and a color (inherited from EarthMaterial).  Specific material properties (and CompoundMaterial nesting) are available in GeoSciML Extension.</p>

<clause id="_ab7d1f71-38d6-1b7e-3a7b-02b18ac03c63" obligation="normative">
2



001041_9f41e531-c0e2-2445-184f-642f2217aa58STANDOC_48
(generic warning) Hanging paragraph in clause
<clause id="_9f41e531-c0e2-2445-184f-642f2217aa58" obligation="normative">
<title id="_18b68cb7-7f41-c983-064f-1c438734b083">GeologicEvent</title>
<p id="_03ab30d9-a5ac-2174-c15a-2ad1a39f304b">A GeologicEvent is an identifiable event during which one or more geological processes act to modify geological entities.  It may have a specified geologic age (numeric age or GeochologicEraTerm) and may have specified environments and processes. An example might be a cratonic uplift event during which erosion, sedimentation, and volcanism all take place.</p>

<p id="_b8704e3e-ba70-d732-9140-8dbd9b27ddf0">Because associated processes are incompatible, a single event cannot be shared between DisplacementEvent, AlterationDescription of MetamorphicDescription (a process associated to DisplacementEvent does not apply to AlterationDescription). </p>
2



001090_915d7765-9695-6838-ceef-69c8d67039fdSTANDOC_48
(generic warning) Hanging paragraph in clause
<clause id="_915d7765-9695-6838-ceef-69c8d67039fd" obligation="normative">
<title id="_46276675-7de0-356e-01e9-e8d9c99bb17d">NumericAgeRange</title>
<p id="_ad888576-5559-7a79-b191-2a290be1140c">The NumericAgeRange class represents an absolute age assignment using numeric measurement results.</p>

<clause id="_c9e7ed7e-815a-1337-e1b3-d2c7ca0af20b" obligation="normative">
2



001111_da419a8c-be72-ea40-0d91-302bb867f1d9STANDOC_48
(generic warning) Hanging paragraph in clause
<clause id="_da419a8c-be72-ea40-0d91-302bb867f1d9" obligation="normative">
<title id="_185dc39f-d873-860f-34f3-ef02f09ef817">Geologic Structure</title>
<p id="_ad3598c7-1866-083c-0a9f-65fba1905b88">Geologic Structure is a package of classes to describe GeologicStructures which are a configuration of matter in the Earth based on describable inhomogeneity, pattern, or fracture in an EarthMaterial.  The scale of geological structures ranges from microscopic (micron-scale) to megascopic (km-scale). Examples of such inhomogeneities include fractures, mineral grain boundaries, and boundaries between parts of the rock with different particle geometry (texture) or composition.</p>

<p id="_a208fd22-bf71-253c-2618-63e9a38cd3ba">GeologicStructure is grounded in relationships between parts of a rock or rock body. As used here, it includes sedimentary structures. The identity of a GeologicStructure is independent of the material that is the substrate for the structure although there are almost always strong dependencies between the nature of the earth material substrate and the kinds of geological structure that may be present.</p>
2



001128_2999043e-d2fa-22e1-237d-9609c631295bSTANDOC_48
(generic warning) Hanging paragraph in clause
<clause id="_2999043e-d2fa-22e1-237d-9609c631295b" obligation="normative">
<title id="_d7b901e9-a2c5-3976-f461-e89b8ce2b057">Contact</title>
<p id="_fd9915d6-01b4-7ef9-b72d-6e0c0d071ca4">A contact is a general concept representing any kind of surface separating two geologic units, including primary boundaries such as depositional contacts, all kinds of unconformities, intrusive contacts, and gradational contacts, as well as faults that separate geologic units.</p>

<figure id="_ab82e902-6093-f105-9f80-e618bacd5546" anchor="img_contact_context_diagram" width="601">
2



001147_d044fe97-0d8f-8189-e1a9-f26776d5f44bSTANDOC_48
(generic warning) Hanging paragraph in clause
<clause id="_d044fe97-0d8f-8189-e1a9-f26776d5f44b" obligation="normative">
<title id="_329cb0b6-6efa-3485-7cd5-37f66f78acc1">Fold*</title>
<p id="_033c51b9-c823-2127-f367-c88e00a51132">A fold is formed by one or more systematically curved layers, surfaces, or lines in a rock body. A fold denotes a structure formed by the deformation of a geologic structure, such as a contact which the original undeformed geometry is presumed, to form a structure that may be described by the translation of an abstract line (the fold axis) parallel to itself along some curvilinear path (the fold profile). Folds have a hinge zone (zone of maximum curvature along the surface) and limbs (parts of the deformed surface not in the hinge zone).  Folds are described by an axial surface, hinge line, profile geometry, the solid angle between the limbs, and the relationships between adjacent folded surfaces if the folded structure is a Layering fabric. </p>

<figure id="_2c8f762d-b133-6d2c-d57c-b041eb6e42d2" anchor="img_fold_context_diagram" width="601">
2



001166_a785f6fb-6e4e-23fe-9856-c8998d0ac4b8STANDOC_48
(generic warning) Hanging paragraph in clause
<clause id="_a785f6fb-6e4e-23fe-9856-c8998d0ac4b8" obligation="normative">
<title id="_4da82b65-4c3c-b75b-8a26-fca7a2a0d425">Foliation</title>
<p id="_4d8daab4-9cf4-4dd1-99f5-9757192f5824">A foliation is a planar arrangement of textural or structural features in any type of rock.  It includes any of a wide variety of penetrative planar geological structures that may be present in a rock.  Examples include schistosity, mylonitic foliation, penetrative bedding structure (lamination), and cleavage.  Following the proposed definition of gneiss by the NADM Science Language Technical Team [12], penetrative planar foliation defined by layers &gt; 5 mm thick is considered Layering.</p>

<p id="_76b5236e-ab7f-973c-0b8c-c873fc64fc6a">Bedding is a fabric representing the average orientation of paleodepositional surface and should be encoded through the foliationType property.  It might apply to bedding that is layering or a foliation without layering (e.g. clast alignment in amalgamated beds).</p>
2

(generic warning) Hanging paragraph in clause
<clause id="_b1d797be-7ad6-1017-8148-93eb28a59488" obligation="normative">
<title id="_57efc911-3a66-c08a-f1f2-378c471adc95">ShearDisplacementStructure</title>
<p id="_7144e4d5-ba48-9a63-5c7b-0730e91500cf">A shear displacement structure includes all brittle to ductile style structures along which displacement has occurred, from a simple, single ‘planar’ brittle or ductile surface to a fault system comprised of tens of strands of both brittle and ductile nature. This structure may have some significant thickness (a deformation zone) and have an associated body of deformed rock that may be considered a deformation unit (which geologicUnitType is ‘DeformationUnit’) which can be associated to the ShearDisplacementStructure using GeologicFeatureRelation from the GeoSciML Extension package (8.5.1.2).</p>

<figure id="_428bce5c-02b0-252d-ee4a-f1c3286e7aa2" anchor="img_ShearDisplacementStructure_context_diagram" width="601">
2

<title id="_bf5f8740-1ee4-6ab4-66d6-85e48414f3a7">Geomorphology</title>
<p id="_3f53b885-d0ce-9eff-7eb9-c9d8509089b0">The Geomorphology sub-package describes features that comprise the shape and nature of the Earth’s land surface (i.e., landforms).  These landforms may be created by natural or anthropogenic processes.</p>

<figure id="_c3930112-8fbf-24cd-9a66-2c94e01b2cf6" anchor="img_Geomorphologic_feature_summary_diagram" width="601">
2



001215_a97cb6a0-351e-68da-3358-f2a766201de7STANDOC_48
(generic warning) Hanging paragraph in clause
<clause id="_a97cb6a0-351e-68da-3358-f2a766201de7" obligation="normative">
<title id="_b102b578-2a87-7ae3-319f-7193e7247026">GeomorphologicFeature</title>
<p id="_25051416-6483-844a-74ee-e5137d9c71d6">A geomorphologic feature is a kind of GeologicFeature describing the shape and nature of the Earth’s land surface.  These landforms may be created by natural Earth processes (e.g., river channel, beach, moraine or mountain) or through human (anthropogenic) activity (e.g., dredged channel, reclaimed land, mine waste dumps).  In GeoSciML, the geomorphologic feature is modelled as a feature related (through unitDescription property) to a GeologicUnit that composes the form.</p>

<figure id="_6c215115-3482-cc81-05d9-5711f0e68fde" anchor="img_partial_encoding_of_landform" width="601">
2



001236_c7ec03f9-6a7c-57d3-cc0a-c3fcddc77fb4STANDOC_48
(generic warning) Hanging paragraph in clause
<clause id="_c7ec03f9-6a7c-57d3-cc0a-c3fcddc77fb4" obligation="normative">
<title id="_a17aeaad-6183-3213-5a51-9ce6a6084178">NaturalGeomorphologicFeature</title>
<p id="_d41f4b3f-f4c4-3d3e-e395-081d19c19805">A natural geomorphologic feature is a geomorphologic feature (i.e., landform) that has been created by natural Earth processes. For example, river channel, beach ridge, caldera, canyon, moraine or mud flat.</p>

<clause id="_cad61f63-7c08-8250-06f8-c4d0deee0153" obligation="normative">
2



001251_b74e563e-1368-db93-ba1c-b86bc3df688dSTANDOC_48
(generic warning) Hanging paragraph in clause
<clause id="_b74e563e-1368-db93-ba1c-b86bc3df688d" obligation="normative">
<title id="_56d4dc4c-4ef5-ed18-8685-28a9f3b54a64">AnthropogenicGeomorphologicFeature</title>
<p id="_a6348aa2-754f-3e88-165c-4ede146513e4">An anthropogenic geomorphologic feature is a geomorphologic feature (i.e., landform) which has been created by human activity.  For example, a dredged channel, midden, open pit or reclaimed land.</p>

<clause id="_bfd34753-7e4e-0737-f625-b287ad5e035c" obligation="normative">
2



001262_1352b7d6-b644-1435-0474-80882c6d79aeSTANDOC_48
(generic warning) Hanging paragraph in clause
<clause id="_1352b7d6-b644-1435-0474-80882c6d79ae" obligation="normative">
<title id="_b827afce-dcb3-f415-09be-e186080daad2">Collection</title>
<p id="_fca92a10-a00f-69d2-342d-cf574da7633a">A GeoSciML collection is a convenience class to manage sets of features or type instances.  A collection contains classes that facilitate the structuring of WFS response documents and other application uses.  </p>

<figure id="_cf914c16-fa0b-9131-e7e9-aa4c247ba1b3" anchor="img_GSML_collection_summary_diagram" width="601">
2



001270_8e19ad0b-b67e-696f-49d7-14fa1c22ead7STANDOC_48
(generic warning) Hanging paragraph in clause
<clause id="_8e19ad0b-b67e-696f-49d7-14fa1c22ead7" obligation="normative">
<title id="_6e7cadf9-1c71-261d-9510-44f4bf8d53a0">GSML</title>
<p id="_bcb9240e-75ce-7a42-0d06-a4d68f40885d">GSML is a collection class grouping a set of features or types which are members of this collection.  A collectionType property provides context or purpose.</p>

<clause id="_673d3bb5-df41-d9e7-3bff-ac69eecaedad" obligation="normative">
2

<title id="_0f508f6e-c7f1-4126-7808-d1c76262b8b4">GeoSciML data types</title>
<p id="_a7b9015b-52bb-336f-0ec2-cc45845c35ac">GeoSciML Data is a package of data types that describes the planar or linear orientation of a geologic feature using conventions used in geology. They allow specifying direction by a numerical direction vector (e.g., dip/dip direction), or as a description (e.g., compass point (NE), or other text — “toward fold hinge”, “below”).  An additional GSML_QuantityRange class extends SWE::QuantityRange to allow upper and lower values in a numerical range to be delivered as two separate attributes. This is to facilitate query operations on upper and lower values by providing explicit names for these values (which are otherwise encoded as anonymous members of an array in SWE common).</p>

<figure id="_896b1519-44d4-e5d1-39a2-88a92b987b2c" anchor="img_Summary_diagram_of_specialised_GeoSciML_data_types" width="601">

001329_9f7d00e4-5d26-dbb4-7278-c09ca2f6e0c3STANDOC_48
(generic warning) Hanging paragraph in clause
<clause id="_9f7d00e4-5d26-dbb4-7278-c09ca2f6e0c3" obligation="normative">
<title id="_b2769dc7-9ccc-f7d0-f58b-00399ec71f11">GSML_GeometricDescriptionValue</title>
<p id="_d682fd97-5b54-a7fe-f81b-0ab5dd8ff231">GSML_GeometricDescriptionValue is a special abstract data type for descriptions of planar or linear orientations of a geologic feature.   Different subtypes allow specifying direction by direction vector (e.g. dip/dip direction), compass point (e.g.  NE), or description (e.g. “toward fold hinge”, “below’).</p>

<clause id="_5741930a-4588-e0aa-ef47-ce95d5ff2ee1" obligation="normative">

<clause id="_46e17fcf-f548-957d-86ad-6a0bdd99932e" obligation="normative">
<title id="_1970ed71-94f5-852e-4fbb-d7c784669116">GSML_PlanarOrientation</title>
<p id="_00b051d7-7340-5e5c-2862-f071ea5465c3">A planar orientation is composed of two values; the azimuth (a compass point) and a dip (the angle from the horizontal).  Polarity of the plane indicates whether the planar orientation is associated with a directed feature that is overturned, upright, vertical, etc.  There are several conventions to encode a planar orientation and this specification does not impose one but provides a convention property to report it. It must be noted that allowance for different conventions makes manipulation of the data more difficult. Therefore it is recommended that user communities adopt a single measurement convention.</p>

<requirement id="_f2c94d94-5940-651b-afb3-a20e0602eaf7" anchor="req_gsml-basic_plane-pol-dip-az-not-null" model="ogc"> <identifier>/req/gsml-basic/plane-pol-dip-az-not-null</identifier> <component id="_f31fd014-e121-6950-5d9f-35ad9e5d2dd4" class="part"> <p id="_b9ad2e14-7aa3-784e-c0c7-8294995e212c">At least one of polarity, azimuth or dip SHALL not be null.</p>
2



001377_cbe050d4-eeac-e674-7bb4-ba55037a043aSTANDOC_48
(generic warning) Hanging paragraph in clause
<clause id="_cbe050d4-eeac-e674-7bb4-ba55037a043a" obligation="normative">
<title id="_52bf197f-8e87-bd95-b922-77351f830a0e">GSML_LinearOrientation</title>
<p id="_a34a8e8a-1ba6-71a3-bb9e-3d84a378a70d">A linear orientation is composed of a trend (the compass orientation of the line) and a plunge (the angle from the horizontal).  This vector may be oriented (pointing in a specific direction) or not.</p>

<requirement id="_0fced6fd-f763-fd32-0603-37838e77a95d" anchor="req_gsml-basic_linear-trend-plunge-not-null" model="ogc"> <identifier>/req/gsml-basic/linear-trend-plunge-not-null</identifier> <component id="_65895848-125e-63fd-7db8-a0f2dd953ae3" class="part"> <p id="_b524b673-1cbd-3089-d8ea-fd63f490648d">At least one of plunge or trend SHALL not be null.</p>
2



001403_f4078331-27c0-550e-67ac-6f798d228d4eSTANDOC_48
(generic warning) Hanging paragraph in clause
<clause id="_f4078331-27c0-550e-67ac-6f798d228d4e" obligation="normative">
<title id="_14a393da-6d5e-7373-fc94-a027886fae21">GSML_Vector</title>
<p id="_606e31a0-ed83-29e1-8c1f-e7f2cd2ed0d8">A GSML_Vector is a data type representing a linear orientation with a magnitude (a quantity assigned to this vector).   If the magnitude is unknown, a GSML_LinearOrientation (8.4.6.3) shall be used.</p>

<clause id="_5ea59f66-36a8-25ca-a935-d5b016f67b2b" obligation="normative">
2

<title id="_c8602973-3387-da44-6b8c-d3b649128172">GSML_QuantityRange</title>
<p id="_c6aa64ff-2760-365f-53fe-1057c812c187">GSML_QuantityRange is a specialization of SWE Common QuantiytyRange (OGC 08-094r1, Clause 7.2.13)  where lower and upper values are made explicit.  SWE::QuantityRange uses an array of values (RealPair, see Clause OGC 08-094r1,7.2.1) where the lowest value is the first element and the highest the second.  This convenience data type has been created as an alternative encoding for implementations that do no support encoding of arrays in a single field (e.g. DBF) or reference to elements in string encoded arrayshttps://docs.ogc.org/is/16-008/16-008.html#_ftnref3[<underline>[3]</underline>] (eg. Filter Encoding Specification 2.0 – OGC 09-029r2).</p>

<figure id="_83c5bd74-675b-0101-1504-315e11daf12f" anchor="img_Context_diagram_for_QuantityRange" width="260">

<title id="_cabdc79c-4344-ca88-7179-d45c44739adf">GeologicFeatureRelation</title>
<p id="_cd71e44a-82a2-e2e2-bcda-fe348a2da476">The GeologicFeatureRelation class defines the general structure used to define relationships between any GeoSciML feature types.  Relationships are always binary and directional.  There is always a single source and a single target.  The relationship is always defined from the perspective of the Source and is generally an active verb. </p>

<p id="_6339e823-1647-b335-8e5d-17e7c15e60a4">Example:  a Source may point to an intrusive igneous rock unit.  In this case, the Target would point to the appropriate host rock body and the relationship attribute would be ‘intrudes’.  Other appropriate relationship attributes might include: overlies, offsets, crosscuts, folds, etc.</p>
2



001677_f440147f-e00e-45e4-004d-ca5790f5e3b1STANDOC_48
(generic warning) Hanging paragraph in clause
<clause id="_f440147f-e00e-45e4-004d-ca5790f5e3b1" obligation="normative">
<title id="_8deb53ca-453d-0ff7-b89c-264f15d469c2">MaterialRelation</title>
<p id="_d1a1c507-7e35-f9e8-f3f4-2b406f2a67d5">The MaterialRelation class describes the relationships between constituent parts in an EarthMaterial (e.g. A mineral overgrowth on a phenocryst within a granite). </p>

<p id="_81428426-c0d5-3f0a-1aeb-dd33f628eea7">Example:  Consider an overgrowth of albite on plagioclase in a granite. The Source would originate with the albite constituentPart description.  In this case, the Target would point to the plagioclase constituentPart description and the relationship attribute would be ‘overgrowth’ and the sourceRole is ‘overgrows’.  Other appropriate role attributes might include: crosscuts, replaces, etc. for crosscutting and replacement relationships.  Inverse relationships must be explicitly recorded.</p>
2

<title id="_879af34c-9c18-1de7-ced1-8d2ca939f1c7">EarthMaterialDetails</title>
<p id="_869dba45-495f-8596-c7b7-deb9e749a702">EarthMaterialDescription abstract class is materialised into a series of concrete classes to address various aspects of EarthMaterial descriptions:</p>

<ul id="_4b6ab60c-4bfb-998e-936c-e85f3ec584e4"> <li> <p id="_a21ea7a2-dae7-3cbc-09ab-4b6930cd4814">CompositionDescription</p>
2



001724_9ad90ca6-e1db-ef91-6a87-ff19b6a8515dSTANDOC_48
(generic warning) Hanging paragraph in clause
<clause id="_9ad90ca6-e1db-ef91-6a87-ff19b6a8515d" obligation="normative">
<title id="_cb94c552-cd19-e01e-2237-62f7c2e90c9b">AlterationDescription</title>
<p id="_e21776a5-bdac-dbfc-b50b-c53540d53cd4">image::images/image39.png[Alteration description context diagram.,width=531,height=570]Figure: 37: Alteration description context diagram.</p>

<p id="_1eb109b7-8523-2410-aabf-e80c6c75e99c">AlterationDescription describes aspects of a geologic unit or earth material that are the result of bulk chemical, mineralogical or physical changes related to change in the physical or chemical environment. It includes weathering, supergene alteration, hydrothermal alteration and metasomatic effects not considered metamorphic. For example, a soil profile description would have to be constructed as a GeologicUnit (geologicUnitType = PedologicUnit) with unit parts representing the various horizons in the profile.  Thickness of a weathering profile can be delivered as unitThickness of a GeologicUnit of geologicUnitType equal to “AlterationUnit” (Figure 38).</p>
2

<title id="_92e14514-2dae-ade7-b36c-d463a791c1ab">ChemicalComposition</title>
<p id="_5644e0d1-b8c2-194c-caa5-e1d12e3d1a62">ChemicalComposition is a kind of EarthMaterialDescription that delivers the chemical composition of a geological unit or earth material, as a list of element or oxide concentrations.</p>

<p id="_03b24abd-c3b9-b1c4-6e72-ac8f040f87ca">image::images/image42.png[Chemical composition context diagram.,width=525,height=339]Figure: 40: Chemical composition context diagram.</p>
2

(generic warning) Hanging paragraph in clause

<title id="_b36fcf97-2f77-1f3c-3b50-66cb0e7dfeb7">CompoundMaterialDescription</title>
<p id="_73a10ac1-53b3-6759-b92d-277c77ad66ce">The CompoundMaterialDescription class is a kind of EarthMaterialDescription that provides an extended description of a compound earth material (i.e., rocks and unconsolidated solid earth materials).</p>

<p id="_6bdd7fd7-2108-b9d4-8539-f20bf3eff229">image::images/image43.png[Compound material description context diagram.,width=601,height=533]Figure: 41: Compound material description context diagram.</p>
2



001803_71da11fe-6d45-2117-eb69-945d62947898STANDOC_48
(generic warning) Hanging paragraph in clause
<clause id="_71da11fe-6d45-2117-eb69-945d62947898" obligation="normative">
<title id="_4619c7ba-af54-dcde-ee92-a82adb310a7c">ParticleGeometryDescription</title>
<p id="_afd89cad-f4b6-3dcc-af6c-55194eb83f78">ParticleGeometryDescription describes particles in a CompoundMaterial independent of their relationship to each other or their orientation. It is distinguished from Fabric in that the ParticleGeometryDescription remains constant if the material is disaggregated into its constituent particles, whereas Fabric is lost if the material is disaggregated.  Properties include the particle size (grainsize), particle sorting (size distribution, e.g., well sorted, poorly sorted, bimodal sorting), particle shape (surface rounding or crystal face development, e.g., well rounded, euhedral, anhedral), and particle aspect ratio (e.g., elongated, platy, bladed, compact, acicular).</p>

<p id="_2dcc88d3-6647-5675-7fb3-90098449cab5">image::images/image44.png[ParticleGeometry context diagram.,width=273,height=453]Figure: 42: ParticleGeometry context diagram.</p>
2



001848_2300ccfb-e22b-4e9a-d3c4-dbaf63c43b99STANDOC_48
(generic warning) Hanging paragraph in clause
<clause id="_2300ccfb-e22b-4e9a-d3c4-dbaf63c43b99" obligation="normative">
<title id="_879bd11e-6583-c5a7-4ae9-a50f9e1db6ce">ConstituentPart</title>
<p id="_20257fac-cc6c-7a79-266c-9bee765cc6d8">image::images/image45.png[ConstituentPart context diagram.,width=601,height=691]Figure: 43: ConstituentPart context diagram.</p>

<p id="_6c659d1f-a30e-8fce-b2e5-82051bc57408">The ConstituentPart class describes how Earth materials may be made up of other Earth materials, including the proportion of the constituent part in the whole (e.g., 20%, minor, dominant); and the role that the constituent plays in the whole (e.g., matrix, groundmass, framework, phenocryst, xenolith, vein).</p>
2



001872_789e528a-4185-813f-99a7-4432aa8d0244STANDOC_48
(generic warning) Hanging paragraph in clause
<clause id="_789e528a-4185-813f-99a7-4432aa8d0244" obligation="normative">
<title id="_7854de7e-bf69-e5a9-ea9f-3834d8654637">FabricDescription</title>
<p id="_74fcbc9c-87c7-769f-298b-5f4e0ca118f4">The FabricDescription data type describes all types of fabrics associated with a CompoundMaterial (i.e., tectonic, metamorphic, sedimentary, igneous fabrics or textures).  It denotes a pattern, defined by one or more CompoundMaterial constituents, that is present throughout a rock body when considered at some scale.  FabricDescription is defined based on the average configuration of many constituents.  Penetrative fabric denotes that these constituents are distributed throughout the rock volume at the scale of observation [15], and are repeated at distances that are small relative to the scale of the whole, such that they can be considered to pervade the whole uniformly ([19] p. 21-24; [7] p. 73; [10],[15]).</p>

<p id="_6b1e7456-cdc0-2367-2c78-bac3b5ea6a7e">FabricDescription is distinguished from ParticleGeometry based on the criteria that particle geometry is preserved if a CompoundMaterial is disaggregated, while FabricDescription is not defined if the material is disaggregated.</p>
2



001893_0d0fc2e1-dcc3-b33f-5283-b492347e45acSTANDOC_48

<title id="_f3fff930-4fc2-fc63-6738-98d96960628b">MetamorphicDescription</title>
<p id="_933a534b-0a3a-5730-2275-db76d98ec14e">The data type MetamorphicDescription describes the character of metamorphism applied to a CompoundMaterial or GeologicUnit using one or more properties including estimated intensity (grade; e.g. high grade, low grade), characteristic metamorphic mineral assemblages (facies; e.g., greenschist, amphibolite), peak P-T estimates, and protolith material if known.  A MetamorphicDescription provides a link to the GeologicEvent associated to the metamorphic event.</p>

<p id="_abac32be-2584-3e1a-1926-cb3637f12dcf">image::images/image48.png[Metamorphic description context diagram.,width=601,height=639]Figure: 46: Metamorphic description context diagram.</p>
2



001946_acef35c9-80a9-bca5-785b-944cb5610a4bSTANDOC_48
(generic warning) Hanging paragraph in clause
<clause id="_acef35c9-80a9-bca5-785b-944cb5610a4b" obligation="normative">
<title id="_dcd4f5ad-798c-cffb-0bdd-e55bfea6ac35">PhysicalDescription</title>
<p id="_078e91ed-2ce9-bfec-c2ee-1b4791d6ca1c">PhysicalDescription is a class that describes the numeric physical properties of a geologic unit (GeologicUnit 8.4.1.3), earth material (EarthMaterial 8.4.1.6), or geologic structure (GeologicStructure 8.4.3.1). (e.g., density, porosity, magnetic susceptibility, remanent magnetism).  These properties are modelled here as scalar numeric values (SWE::Quantity).</p>

<p id="_da01ef85-d100-6a62-0fc1-839693249393">Vector and tensor physical properties are considered to be more applicable to located observations and should be delivered as OM_Observations with associated geologic unit or geologic structure features.  Since PhysicalProperty can be an arbitrary property, it satisfies the requirements of clause 7.2.2.8 or OGC 10-004r3 that states that “<em>The observed property shall be a phenomenon associated with the feature-of-interest.</em>”, and hence any GeologicUnit, GeologicStructure are valid features of interest for any OM_Observation.</p>
2

<title id="_44a918a8-0c24-da17-f81d-1c514db0d420">RockMaterialDescription</title>
<p id="_c662ebb2-e936-efcc-3fce-fe4bc13dde80">RockMaterialDescription provides extended description of RockMaterial.</p>

<p id="_94c92db6-0139-ef02-5ba8-578475e68eac">image::images/image52.png[Rock material description context diagram.,width=271,height=730]Figure: 50: Rock material description context diagram.</p>

<title id="_80abb279-3888-ed69-4cb3-e35476c961c4">GeologicAgeDetails</title>
<p id="_ca794671-6bfd-faa1-6ae6-4c8f87a98b1b">GeologicEventDescription provides extended description of geologic events through links to GeochronologicEras in the GeologicTimescale model.  GeoSciML Basic provides terms whereas GeoSciML Extension provides a fuller ontology to describe geochronology (see 8.6).</p>

<p id="_9ba3186f-1e93-6502-c48d-e371886b19b3">image::images/image53.png[GeologicAgeDetails summary diagram.,width=548,height=726]Figure: 51: GeologicAgeDetails summary diagram.</p>

<title id="_fe4bf504-816d-7ea5-dfeb-cd70a2aacbcc">GeologicStructureDetails</title>
<p id="_ce4bd65c-38fd-3474-375c-720696bfabac">The Geologic Structure Details package provides for extended descriptions of geologic structures. </p>

<p id="_38238c24-9aa1-aa53-3f8a-7dba7a1cfb19">image::images/image54.png[Summary diagram for GeologicStructureDetails.,width=601,height=471]Figure: 52: Summary diagram for GeologicStructureDetails.</p>

<title id="_6d6ad33f-6566-77b4-d44f-0bb7c218a9d1">ContactDescription</title>
<p id="_3de7e298-7362-d8ba-6bea-9ac69ea18a4e">The ContactDescription provides extended descriptive properties of a geologic contact.  If the contact type is ChronostratigraphicBoundary, it can be associated with a geochronologic (i.e., time zone) boundary that may correlate with it.</p>

<p id="_01bf18c1-2b6e-24cb-652b-e241badded11">image::images/image55.png[ContactDescription context diagram.,width=601,height=543]Figure: 53: ContactDescription context diagram.</p>

<title id="_b42b501b-43ae-f80f-6501-1c3598456aca">DisplacementEvent</title>
<p id="_4db8fdb9-417a-3d87-0195-ec35a1854eb4">A displacement event is a description of the age, environment and process of a shear displacement event.</p>

<p id="_285882ac-033a-9a95-496c-4056aa60895d">image::images/image56.png[DisplacementEvent context diagram,width=391,height=575]Figure: 54: DisplacementEvent context diagram</p>
2



002045_9871fc31-5a90-af7d-cbe5-dc1f62515229STANDOC_48
(generic warning) Hanging paragraph in clause
<clause id="_9871fc31-5a90-af7d-cbe5-dc1f62515229" obligation="normative">
<title id="_61de2bd0-96c0-03c9-63dd-01ed08662a2e">Layering</title>
<p id="_74718a13-e825-1931-0452-a34a8ce01ce7">A planar foliation is defined by a tabular succession of layers &gt; 5 mm thick. This definition is based on the proposed definition of gneiss by the NADM Science Language Technical Team [13].  The GeologicStructure characteristic of gneiss is layering.</p>

<p id="_5c692a5b-4272-9042-41b6-f739c1862a6c">image::images/image57.png[Layering context diagram,width=552,height=440]Figure: 55: Layering context diagram</p>
2

<title id="_3df09af8-191c-0204-fdd7-c84cfaec25db">SeparationValue</title>
<p id="_8ef8d611-c3fe-2521-0ec9-1968d7c4ff38">SeparationValue is a kind of DisplacementValue that describes the amount of separation displacement across a structure.</p>

<clause id="_aadb9b35-5d3b-0acc-16d5-ff8c903e3262" obligation="normative">
2



002094_76e7f283-feca-592c-b2b2-284bf1bc17b7STANDOC_48
(generic warning) Hanging paragraph in clause
<clause id="_76e7f283-feca-592c-b2b2-284bf1bc17b7" obligation="normative">
<title id="_999581ca-958d-48b9-4927-83f423fadd3f">NetSlipValue</title>
<p id="_9bc84488-9159-1445-98b0-68b7df848c7d">NetSlipValue is a kind of DisplacementValue that describes the total amount of slip displacement along a structure.</p>

<clause id="_767cc8a5-ac5d-491e-9d2f-de6525b2a9dd" obligation="normative">
2



002109_4588fe2a-f872-369a-ca19-f9739e3b2b4eSTANDOC_48
(generic warning) Hanging paragraph in clause
<clause id="_4588fe2a-f872-369a-ca19-f9739e3b2b4e" obligation="normative">
<title id="_ddbd3e15-9364-d05f-33d9-cbacf192f694">SlipComponents</title>
<p id="_fc18804c-8c32-41f4-2af8-8422be7a29a5">SlipComponents is a kind of DisplacementValue that is a representation of slip as a vector resolved into components within a reference frame in which horizontal axes are parallel and perpendicular to the strike of the fault.  At least one of heave, horizontalSlip, or throw must not be null.</p>

<table id="_3f1e5711-c7fb-bfe1-3328-c185c25fd74d" width="100%"> <thead> <tr id="_d10cdc5a-9c2d-ba1b-d512-d512a34d476a"> <th id="_32a3168a-cadb-e45a-ff30-f7ca9f49f882" valign="middle" align="left"> <strong>Requirement /req/gsml4-extension/slipComponents-slip</strong> </th>
2

<title id="_a5869db6-79ff-f049-7904-8003a93f9a8e">FoldDescription</title>
<p id="_762cd774-e0e4-e57f-74e4-582da56909d3">FoldDescription is an extended descriptive property of a fold structure.</p>

<p id="_bd5a49c3-26ca-b5b1-68e1-43fd66e2969c">image::images/image59.png[FoldDescription context diagram.,width=601,height=557]Figure: 57: FoldDescription context diagram.</p>
2

<title id="_eb614933-4d43-ab1f-6f97-5950a05e5f34">FoldSystem</title>
<p id="_56b47ae8-aebf-9c80-ad48-c94b9be296d4">A FoldSystem is a collection of congruent folds (axis and axial surface are parallel) produced by the same tectonic event. It is sometimes referred to as a “fold train”.</p>

<p id="_bf49931b-77e8-fc46-2a07-a8a498d5d157">image::images/image60.png[FoldSystem context diagram.,width=601,height=611]Figure: 58: FoldSystem context diagram.</p>
2

<title id="_fae7aa56-60d6-6860-c0f5-05ad2ab01423">FoliationDescription</title>
<p id="_901db08d-a234-398d-bdbe-a5de98101c97">FoliationDescription provides extended descriptive properties for a foliation structure.</p>

<p id="_5e9bd15c-21c3-8340-713e-870d9f6d887f">image::images/image61.png[FoliationDescription context diagram.,width=601,height=644]Figure: 59: FoliationDescription context diagram.</p>
2

<title id="_12d7c7de-1761-e488-47cd-41abae871c0c">ShearDisplacementStructureDescription</title>
<p id="_30f2cdf1-43c6-818c-e443-c96893e42fad">ShearDisplacementStructureDescription provides extended descriptive properties of a shear displacement structure (i.e., fault or shear) defined in 8.4.3.5 by extending the abstract property block ShearDisplacementStructureAbstractDescription.</p>

<p id="_5a7ce768-516f-7ad1-7919-535a9f71ac4b">image::images/image62.png[ShearDisplacementStructureDescription context diagram.,width=601,height=447]Figure: 60: ShearDisplacementStructureDescription context diagram.</p>
2

<title id="_2bace503-d6dd-91e0-fe3d-efccc15c6244">GeologicUnitDetails</title>
<p id="_94d83210-d0b9-a933-0c46-69768e955463">The GeologicUnitDetails package provides for extended description of geologic unit features (8.4.1.3).</p>

<p id="_c8e10a0e-3a0c-1061-f231-083ea7edcb6d">image::images/image63.png[GeologicUnitDetails,width=338,height=726]Figure: 61: GeologicUnitDetails</p>

<p id="_490a504a-b1a4-cc37-5df9-e6f75b2efd51">GeologicUnitDescription provides for extended description of the characteristics of a geologic unit (8.4.1.3).</p>

<clause id="_4c1e243f-a349-9224-1a4a-8fee7984115b" obligation="normative">
2

<p id="_ff8fb173-4d39-2495-6e67-28de22f2fb38">BeddingDescription provides a detailed description of the bedding characteristics of a geologic unit.</p>

<clause id="_ed13e140-4abc-b63e-c617-fee0f4f6d4ee" obligation="normative">

<title id="_e02cbcba-2158-24d5-fa32-bccc4700c461">Global Boundary Stratotype Sections and Points (GSSP)</title>
<p id="_1d54ef38-2c41-5e4b-c293-0acd040d9c20">The GSSP model describes “Global Boundary Stratotype Sections and Points” as defined by the IUGS International Commission on Stratigraphy.</p>

<p id="_3f3075e1-fd76-8405-4333-0091a630dfc7">image::images/image66.png[Global Boundary Stratotype Sections and Points.,width=601,height=457]Figure: 64: Global Boundary Stratotype Sections and Points.</p>
2



002412_02ed0ebb-0e4e-11d4-af05-46d4b54af3d1STANDOC_48
(generic warning) Hanging paragraph in clause
<clause id="_02ed0ebb-0e4e-11d4-af05-46d4b54af3d1" obligation="normative">
<title id="_14539628-a32d-cb3b-be1f-beaa89c30592">StratigraphicPoint</title>
<p id="_6e0ebd59-6dc3-24f8-17e3-88d4c69c8c4b">A point in the stratigraphic record used to define a geochronologic boundary or point in geologic time.</p>

<p id="_25365e7b-178c-8c77-4d09-331a4f2068b9">image::images/image67.png[Stratigraphic points context diagram,width=346,height=526]Figure: 65: Stratigraphic points context diagram</p>
2



002439_ea344b39-9dfb-893d-5c2b-ceab1fad8f16STANDOC_48
(generic warning) Hanging paragraph in clause
<clause id="_ea344b39-9dfb-893d-5c2b-ceab1fad8f16" obligation="normative">
<title id="_07b6d04b-88d2-4a3b-289b-2c776ebc0116">StratigraphicSection</title>
<p id="_349d01c4-2975-e61b-1d6f-1572ec602c46">A sampled section of the stratigraphic record used to define a period in geologic time.</p>

<p id="_5bcf4743-41f2-fe6c-57e5-498a9b7be948">image::images/image68.png[Stratigraphic sections context diagram.,width=531,height=574]Figure: 66: Stratigraphic sections context diagram.</p>
2



002467_a8bd9ad8-0c33-6566-9362-bbbee0e356bcSTANDOC_48
(generic warning) Hanging paragraph in clause
<clause id="_a8bd9ad8-0c33-6566-9362-bbbee0e356bc" obligation="normative">
<title id="_8b948996-4d35-522a-9568-084ef2510d02">TemporalReferenceSystem</title>
<p id="_7302477a-a69c-55ad-7a84-eaefa0994c55">This package is an extension of ISO19108 Temporal Schema and describes geologic eras and the relationships between them.</p>

<p id="_3358faf2-3ddf-9738-65a4-fa0022cfabf6">image::images/image69.png[Temporal Reference System summary diagram.,width=601,height=710]Figure: 67: Temporal Reference System summary diagram.</p>
2



002473_bf8a5d1c-a194-ede6-dacd-f7a93778b31fSTANDOC_48
(generic warning) Hanging paragraph in clause
<clause id="_bf8a5d1c-a194-ede6-dacd-f7a93778b31f" obligation="normative">
<title id="_769906e7-6ff7-8a8c-10e8-b10180cebf5d">TimeOrdinalReferenceSystem</title>
<p id="_3bc63aa5-e83e-f04c-3f4e-443d5d80735d">TimeOrdinalReferenceSystem is a time reference system comprised of an ordered set of time periods (time ordinal eras).</p>

<clause id="_ec643a92-4bb2-e7bc-9533-59d56c9b8198" obligation="normative">
2



002488_3af5ba21-c176-3fd1-0a6d-844e15528a88STANDOC_48
(generic warning) Hanging paragraph in clause
<clause id="_3af5ba21-c176-3fd1-0a6d-844e15528a88" obligation="normative">
<title id="_7c83ffe5-d3dc-a511-be94-dc8f204e3a50">TimeOrdinalEra</title>
<p id="_53be0dc5-0bb8-036f-aeeb-f1f1e82b494a">TimeOrdinalEra is a period of time between two time boundaries.  The association of an era with a stratotype is optional.  In the GSSP approach recommended by ICS for the Global Geologic Timescale, Unit Stratotypes are not used.  Rather, the association of an era with geologic units and sections is indirect, via the association of an era with boundaries, which are in turn tied to stratotype points, which occur within host stratotype sections.  TimeOrdinalEra can be composed of other eras and organized into an arbitrarily nested tree.</p>

<clause id="_9521491d-bcc1-8f30-9043-1dd2fb6a6278" obligation="normative">
2

<title id="_3d55c35b-884e-d8a7-944e-5126f2d3688d">TimeOrdinalEraBoundary</title>
<p id="_baea2b5b-177e-5ae0-6fff-7b4b92af4c54">A TimeOrdinalEraBoundary is a point in Earth’s history which bounds a TimeOrdinalEra.</p>

<clause id="_1fad430b-3df4-efb4-3305-4ac41c1df193" obligation="normative">
2

<title id="_30c7dddf-9682-55e8-32de-6d5be6197aaa">Timescale</title>
<p id="_b3e29063-00f2-54dd-5cf1-f1ae40eed1eb">The Timescale package describes geologic time periods (geochronologic eras) and the boundaries between them.</p>

<p id="_429e4606-34e7-a462-d8fe-6ab951bc6a6f">image::images/image70.png[Time scale summary diagram.,width=601,height=515]Figure: 68: Time scale summary diagram.</p>
2

(generic warning) Hanging paragraph in clause
<clause id="_1671e8de-1550-7bd7-ba2a-5b6cf24c5904" obligation="normative">
<title id="_d5d80bce-1318-287e-695f-e4648ea00263">GeochronologicEra</title>
<p id="_d13f21a1-3572-3415-9e43-abf98f0ecaf1">A GeochronologicEra is a period of time between two GeochronologicBoundaries. The association of a GeochronologicEra with a stratotype is optional.  In the GSSP approach recommended by ICS for the Global Geologic Timescale, Unit Stratotypes are not used.  Rather, the association of an era with geologic units and sections is indirect, via the association of an era with boundaries, which are in turn tied to stratotype points, which occur within host stratotype sections.</p>

<p id="_3835c810-3bae-d27b-9b13-3f3fc49ea4f9">image::images/image71.png[GeochronologicEra context diagram.,width=601,height=546]Figure: 69: GeochronologicEra context diagram.</p>
2

(generic warning) Hanging paragraph in clause
<clause id="_22d58c43-e317-5273-0481-c84c1837ede6" obligation="normative">
<title id="_8e772584-9622-c950-5505-26b12c2a970b">GeochronologicBoundary</title>
<p id="_dab130ea-220a-0710-3678-7b424943d3c9">A GeochronologicBoundary is a boundary between two geochronologic time periods.</p>

<p id="_743e8a25-c5cd-bad8-9340-f5e113ea1326">image::images/image72.png[GeochronologicBoundary context diagram.,width=601,height=658]Figure: 70: GeochronologicBoundary context diagram.</p>
2

<title id="_1084d534-1f26-2ad8-0063-1b69011fa6f4">Borehole</title>
<p id="_db827b14-dffc-48da-e64f-eff0abeddb1e">This requirements class describes Borehole and BoreholeInterval and related data types.  This package describes a borehole as a means to sample geologic units underground and thus provide a linear map of the geology.</p>

<p id="_395723af-3f80-3bf1-c9f5-cb590a23caa1">image::images/image77.png[Borehole context diagram.,width=601,height=331]Figure: 75: Borehole context diagram.</p>
2



002725_142ff89d-b889-e772-af34-c0d4b4480ee9STANDOC_48
(generic warning) Hanging paragraph in clause
<clause id="_142ff89d-b889-e772-af34-c0d4b4480ee9" obligation="normative">
<title id="_1bac4e91-e8d5-541e-0429-24f6166556c9">Borehole</title>
<p id="_21a64019-cdee-93f9-e4a6-510045335057">A Borehole is the generalized term for any narrow shaft drilled in the ground, either vertically, horizontally, or inclined.</p>

<clause id="_4043aac6-6e5e-efab-251b-2ed113268064" obligation="normative">
2

<title id="_daf3141d-c800-c69e-5317-f2daf8e51145">DrillingDetails</title>
<p id="_c9bdbbc3-2d6f-73a2-fbef-72e5de12a163">DrillingDetails is a class that captures the description of drilling methods and hole diameters down the drilling path.  Properties that apply to the Borehole as a whole are managed in BoreholeDetails (8.7.1.4).</p>

<p id="_318b0180-bb86-aecf-d949-f5d9b6a8cd93">image::images/image78.png[Drilling details,width=601,height=387]Figure 76: Drilling details</p>
2

<title id="_9ddcd8c9-74a9-30f7-312f-5440dcd35102">BoreholeInterval</title>
<p id="_ca4178b7-e23e-10d0-46fc-7a4bc53584ba">A BoreholeInterval is similar to a MappedFeature (8.4.1.2) whose shape is 1-D interval and uses the SRS of the containing borehole.  The “mappedIntervalBegin” and “mappedIntervalEnd” properties are alternative to the 1D geometry to overcome problems with the delivery and ease of queryability of 1D GML shapes.</p>

<p id="_ab1f5082-c8db-ca17-15d5-0d9416295954">image::images/image79.png[Borehole interval context diagram.,width=601,height=439]Figure: 77: Borehole interval context diagram.</p>
2

<title id="_0f2ee312-1775-e53a-d451-44a9eb8ab1aa">BoreholeDetails</title>
<p id="_36fd5906-3633-494b-598b-a6b515873e05">BoreholeDetails describes borehole-specific index data, often termed “header information”. It contains metadata about the parties involved in the drilling, the storage of drilled material and other information relevant to the borehole as a whole.  Properties that may vary along the borehole path are managed in DrillingDetails (8.7.1.2).</p>

<p id="_0d4c7855-dd7d-9248-5120-41e5dd6104a5">image::images/image82.png[Borehole details context diagram.,width=601,height=570]Figure: 80: Borehole details context diagram.</p>

<title id="_15eb532d-9bc5-2809-410f-41628676458b">OriginPosition</title>
<p id="_34315eda-ee63-db8a-62a1-214cffd4cb79">A borehole OriginPosition is a feature corresponding to the start point of a borehole log.  This may correspond to the borehole collar location (e.g., kelly bush).</p>

<p id="_d6ff9ced-4261-55d2-0e87-e93b28b27ede">image::images/image83.png[Origin position context diagram.,width=518,height=456]Figure: 81: Origin position context diagram.</p>

<title id="_61dbe29f-7c82-3500-56c3-bc4796be83e8">LaboratoryAnalysis</title>
<p id="_36083fba-2590-b359-dccd-378b53e3ec6f">The LaboratoryAnalysis leaf package describes processes, instruments and result quality associated with quantitative analysis of samples.  It is an application of ISO19156 Observations and Measurements with supplemental requirements over some of O&amp;M classes.</p>

<clause id="_509d783f-5dd7-d46b-ffd1-9c6ae7bb3be0" obligation="normative">

<title id="_2e5ccc85-ea6e-3572-d16e-ec0b795cddb5">AnalyticalInstrument</title>
<p id="_bd156ef0-c605-3d24-136d-ef6ac4c2dfab">The analytical instrument is the category of instrument used to perform an analytical measurement or observation.</p>

<p id="_035529ae-8a3b-7f5a-4fc2-dd60428e6fdb">image::images/image87.png[Analytical instrument context diagram.,width=601,height=321]Figure: 85: Analytical instrument context diagram.</p>
2

<title id="_29814168-3191-48df-a059-3f19c8b8cea5">AnalyticalSession</title>
<p id="_3928a127-d8c3-7ed0-250d-bbc30cbabe6f">This feature type describes the time and operator of a particular laboratory analytical session. AnalyticalSession also has associated links to the type of instrument and analytical method used, processing steps applied to data collected during a session, and instrument parameters unique to that session.</p>

<p id="_3dfaeb48-bc6e-85ba-b956-ff5bb8162a84">image::images/image88.png[Analytical session context diagram.,width=601,height=475]Figure: 86: Analytical session context diagram.</p>

<title id="_c8238008-8d75-2245-103a-6ada02f1f437">AnalyticalProcess</title>
<p id="_5b457599-8bd8-7bac-fc4c-f5109536b076">An analytical process is a concrete implementation of OM::OM_Process and describes the steps and methods used in an analytical session.  It links to an analytical session (data acquisition) or a computational process which produce analytical results.</p>

<p id="_16b4c978-517f-7876-75ac-21cb3a3d0912">image::images/image89.png[Analytical process,width=601,height=558]Figure: 87: Analytical process</p>
2

Style override set for ordered list

</li>
<li> <p id="_8adcfca0-ff96-4b69-acba-e4b9ab893fca"> the surface rounding of grains in sedimentary rocks. Roundness is a measure of the sharpness of the edges between surfaces bounding a particle [10] [22].</p>

<title id="_372c37c3-cce9-afcb-235b-1dd8b3c0b7e4">AnalyticalMethod</title>
<p id="_fcb24f18-8344-5603-517b-4b6dee5877a4">The AnalyticalMethod provides the name, and published citation, of the analytical method used in an analytical session.</p>

<p id="_faeb6126-2ce8-06da-c321-0071db9dc6c5">image::images/image90.png[Analytical method,width=526,height=352]Figure: 88: Analytical method</p>

<title id="_89e1d703-57e4-b5e6-5233-b2da59e2400f">Geochronology</title>
<p id="_e417b565-a2cd-12ea-997d-fcf65dd71d96">The Geochronology model allows the delivery of geochronological interpretations by describing:</p>

<ol id="_4c7eae2d-eeca-0af9-4e65-e0285a23dcd3" type="arabic"> <li> <p id="_e1e7901e-8c88-3c8c-c046-fbc112ebddad">a OM::SF_Specimen (e.g., a rock sample)</p>
2



003291_05435ae1-e4cd-1fe6-51d5-d611209ab0c2STANDOC_48
(generic warning) Hanging paragraph in clause
<clause id="_05435ae1-e4cd-1fe6-51d5-d611209ab0c2" obligation="normative">
<title id="_4870f9ee-c0cd-4e53-4948-9487224d21d8">GeochronologicInterpretation</title>
<p id="_cd691915-ece6-e56d-7c8c-68f015b30422">A GeochronologicInterpretation is an interpretation made by a geologist of the age of a specimen made by statistical analysis of a collection of observations.  A geologic specimen may have multiple geochronological interpretations made on it, each related to a different observation/result collection.</p>

<p id="_dc844cdd-8a7c-ae3e-e8e3-52c09d2fd560">image::images/image93.png[Geochronologic interpretation context diagram.,width=596,height=556]Figure: 91: Geochronologic interpretation context diagram.</p>
2



003349_fd911205-0f0b-c3e8-6723-6a4b553f45d8STANDOC_48
(generic warning) Hanging paragraph in clause
<clause id="_fd911205-0f0b-c3e8-6723-6a4b553f45d8" obligation="normative">
<title id="_b43b6d17-4b91-831f-4b8e-ca7e5ec7a882">GeologicSpecimen</title>
<p id="_ba41084c-ddbf-cbf0-0139-10303cf87d72">The GeologicSpecimen package extends the ISO19156 O&amp;M model, and describes processes relevant to the sampling, preparation, and analysis of geologic specimens.</p>

<p id="_62881cd4-39f5-5d09-8b6f-cf7527faa41e">image::images/image94.png[Geologic specimen summary diagram.,width=601,height=534]Figure: 92: Geologic specimen summary diagram.</p>
2



003355_b99baba4-6b88-5c68-e9bb-a9afffb93686STANDOC_48
(generic warning) Hanging paragraph in clause
<clause id="_b99baba4-6b88-5c68-e9bb-a9afffb93686" obligation="normative">
<title id="_5f2bfcb2-f17b-775d-aa73-1367636a02ed">ReferenceSpecimen</title>
<p id="_d03a2adb-18e8-8925-3e43-5eaf41611d7c">A reference specimen is a specimen with known or accepted values of some property.  The citation property describes the location of a published description of these values.  Reference specimens include analytical blanks.  ReferenceSpecimens are used in quality control procedures to assess method reproducibility.</p>

<p id="_1509cc5a-9826-7ddd-f9f9-03e555197128">Analytical results from a reference specimen analysed during an AnalyticalSession are delivered in the same way as the results of other specimens analysed in that session.</p>
2



003374_040ff8d9-f328-965a-c320-dbbe8d595785STANDOC_48
(generic warning) Hanging paragraph in clause
<clause id="_040ff8d9-f328-965a-c320-dbbe8d595785" obligation="normative">
<title id="_1934552a-9ad3-56d5-b322-90a8cac9f7d1">GeologicSpecimenPreparation</title>
<p id="_6eb7be16-9a94-40fd-ced6-2038f83c7e69">GeologicSpecimenPreparation is an extension of ISO Specimen::preparationStep to allow details of preparation steps to be delivered (e.g., filtration and mesh size, chemical additives, crushing methods, drying parameters, etc.).</p>

<p id="_3d94a85b-e9a0-9d9e-7998-8f46c0e6fd63">image::images/image96.png[Geologic specimen preparation context diagram.,width=601,height=497]Figure: 94: Geologic specimen preparation context diagram.</p>
2

<p id="_0324dea1-d65a-294d-fb83-7926e6531339">GeologicSamplingMethod is an implementation of OM::SF_Process to describe the method used to obtain a geologic specimen.</p>

<title id="_35605b9e-42c2-eeb1-a9cc-f187d0ce92ee">GeologicUnitView</title>
<p id="_037da5ea-8a6c-ea49-9c64-6433db94ad2b">image::images/image102.png[GeologicUnitView feature type.,width=302,height=382]Figure: 100: GeologicUnitView feature type.</p>

<p id="_bcef984e-2408-c638-f17d-9004d7d92ae8">GeologicUnitView is a simplified view of a GeoSciML MappedFeature feature with key property values from an associated GeologicUnit.   The GeologicUnitView property values are summarised as labels (unconstrained character strings) or arbitrarily selected classifiers to be used for thematic mapping purposes. The latter are the properties suffixed with “_uri” and will contain URIs referring to controlled concepts in published vocabularies.</p>

<title id="_57f3344b-241f-9d6a-4ca6-9356e4865c06">BoreholeView</title>
<p id="_aba10f56-ec03-b217-a236-77ca0a1f5dfd">BoreholeView is a simplified view of a GeoSciML Borehole. In GeoSciML terms, this will be an instance of a Borehole feature with key property values summarised as labels (unconstrained character strings) or arbitrarily selected classifiers to be used for thematic mapping purposes. The latter are the properties suffixed with “_uri” and will contain URIs referring to controlled concepts in published vocabularies.</p>

<p id="_7b63e964-529c-3eca-9ed5-648e211f0f9b"> </p>

<p id="_3cfe9826-c455-4172-13da-878f0462469d">GeologicSpecimenView is a simplified view of a point-located specimen from GeoSciML GeologicSpecimen (an extension of Observations &amp; Measurements — ISO19156) with key property values summarised as labels (unconstrained character strings) or arbitrarily selected classifiers to be used for thematic mapping purposes. The latter are the properties suffixed with “_uri” and will contain URIs referring to controlled concepts in published vocabularies.</p>

004917_713051db-71b0-879b-b4d4-53af891bd516STANDOC_48
(generic warning) Hanging paragraph in clause
<clause id="_713051db-71b0-879b-b4d4-53af891bd516" obligation="normative">
<title id="_16195c23-3217-d63e-9da0-c53ca9865bcc">SiteObservationView</title>
<p id="_d4ed0049-41ac-eeee-f1fe-c9f83a1aa918">image::images/image108.png[SiteObservationView feature type.,width=287,height=349]Figure: 106: SiteObservationView feature type.</p>

<p id="_a7ac07cd-aed7-c5ad-c167-0ea72be585e7">SiteObservationView is a simplified view of a generally point-located geological observation, like a structural measurement. This is a simplified instance of a sampling geometry from Observations &amp; Measurements (ISO19156) with an associated geological observation. Each tuple should represent a single observation. Key property values are summarised as labels (unconstrained character strings) or arbitrarily selected classifiers to be used for thematic mapping purposes. The latter are the properties suffixed with “_uri” and will contain URIs referring to controlled concepts in published vocabularies.</p>
